cards.text: The tribes of Israel are out claiming the land, one tribe at a time. Now we check in on the tribe of Benjamin. The Jebusites are living in Jerusalem, and they need to be driven out.

cards.question: The Benjamites drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem.

cards.text: So to this day, the Jebusites live right there among the Benjamites. Friend, that's not a move-out. That's a ROOMMATE.
Next up, the house of Joseph, Joseph's descendants. They go up to attack the city of Bethel.

cards.question: The LORD is with the house of Joseph as they attack Bethel.
Before the attack on Bethel, what does the house of Joseph send?
Bethel had an older name. It was formerly known as ___.

cards.text: The spies spot a man coming out of the city. Just a guy stepping outside, and BOOM. He's got company.

cards.question: What do the spies ask the man from Bethel to show them?

answers.text: How to get into the city

cards.text: If he does, they promise to treat him kindly. So he shows them the entrance, and they put the city to the sword.

cards.question: The man who showed them the entrance to Bethel is released, along with all his family.
After Bethel falls, the man goes to the land of the Hittites. What does he do there?

cards.text: And Luz is its name to this day. The man lost his city, so he went and built himself a SEQUEL.
Now Manasseh. Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo and their villages, and Manasseh fails to drive out the people living there.

cards.question: What does the text say about the Canaanites in the towns Manasseh didn't take?

answers.text: They were determined to dwell there
They had made peace with Manasseh
They were hiding in the hills

cards.question: Later, when Israel becomes stronger, what do they do with the Canaanites?

cards.text: Strong enough to put them to work, but they never drive them out completely. That's the snooze button, friend: awake enough to hit it, never actually getting UP.

Then the reports roll in, tribe after tribe: Ephraim in Gezer, Zebulun in Kitron and Nahalol, Asher in Acco, Sidon and five more towns, and Naphtali in Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath. Every one fails to drive them out, and the Canaanites keep living right there among them, some as forced laborers.

cards.question: Then there's the tribe of Dan, up against the Amorites. What do the Amorites do to the Danites?

answers.text: Force them into the hill country
Push them out to the coast

cards.text: They won't even let Dan come down into the plain. That's like moving into your new house and the old owners make you live in the ATTIC.
The Amorites are determined to dwell in Mount Heres, Aijalon and Shaalbim. But then the house of Joseph grows in strength.

cards.question: Once the house of Joseph grows in strength, they drive the Amorites out completely.

cards.text: They press the Amorites into forced labor instead. And the Amorites still have a border of their own, from the Ascent of Akrabbim to Sela and beyond.
Now the scene changes. The angel of the LORD goes up from Gilgal to a place called Bochim, and he has something to say.

cards.question: Speaking as 'I,' the angel of the LORD starts with what was done for Israel. What comes first?

answers.text: Brought them up out of Egypt
Gave them a king to lead them

cards.text: Then the angel says, 'I will never break My covenant with you.' That's the promise. Now comes what Israel was told to do.

cards.question: The angel says Israel was not to make a covenant with the people of this land. Instead, they were to tear down their ___.

cards.text: Then the angel says, 'Yet you have not obeyed My voice. What is this you have done?' Friend, NOBODY hears 'What is this you have done?' and thinks they're about to get a raise.

cards.question: Because Israel didn't obey, what does the angel say 'I will not' do now?

answers.text: Drive out these people before them

cards.question: The angel says the people of the land will be thorns in Israel's sides, and their gods will be a snare.
When the angel of the LORD finishes speaking to all the Israelites, the people lift up their voices and ___.
The people name that place Bochim, and there they offer sacrifices to the LORD.

cards.text: Tears, and then sacrifices to the LORD, right there at Bochim. They heard the hard truth, and they turned toward Him with it.

findings.problem: The right answer "Spies" is one word, while the wrong answers "Priests with the ark" and "A herald with terms" are four words each. The short answer stands out from the other two.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "What does the text say about the Canaanites in the towns Manasseh didn't take?" sounds like a test question about the text. It does not come out of the moment the way Papa Dorin pausing mid-story would.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: The summary card for the repeated reports (1:29-33) goes tribe by tribe and town by town (Ephraim in Gezer, Zebulun in Kitron and Nahalol, Asher in Acco, Sidon and five more, Naphtali in Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath). It should say in a few words what the stretch covers.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

findings.problem: The card says the Canaanites keep living among every tribe. For Asher and Naphtali, the text turns this around: the Asherites and the Naphtalites "lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land" (1:32-33).

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card tells the baker the place is called Bochim. Card 15 later asks whether the people name that place Bochim, so the answer to card 15 is already given away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The card presents "I will never break My covenant with you" as something the angel says now ("Then the angel says... That's the promise"). In the text, the angel is recalling what he said before: "and I said, 'I will never break My covenant with you'" (2:1). The card also leaves out "led you into the land that I had promised to your fathers."

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: "They heard the hard truth, and they turned toward Him with it" adds an interpretation (a turning back, or repentance) that the text never states. The text only says they wept, named the place and offered sacrifices to the LORD.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can add a storyteller's line to carry the moment, like "But the Lord isn't finished with him," as long as it adds no facts.

findings.problem: The question is in the present tense ("the people lift up their voices and ___"), but all three answers are past tense (wept, sang, cheered). The sentence does not read correctly once the blank is filled.
findings.question: Should fill-in-the-blank answers have to fit the question's grammar and tense? If so, should this card read "lifted up their voices and ___", or should the answers be weep, sing and cheer?
